evidence: books/peer-inbound.lisp fn-peer-command, TAKETHIS arm: (if (not (fn-peer-msgid-argp args)) (fn-post-make-result ps (fn-peer-single ps (fn-proto-text * :syntax)) nil) ...) -- no fn-nntp-begin-article-effect, no transfer. RFC 4644 2.5.2: the client sends the article immediately after the command line and 'The server MUST return either a 239 response ... or a 439'.
fix: Statement-first: a TAKETHIS line whose argument is not a Message-ID still enters article mode (the transfer remembers the raw argument); the article is consumed by the wire machine and answered 439 echoing the argument (RFC 4644 2.5.1/2.5.2), never submitted to the owner, never remembered in the refused-offer memory. Keystone: after any TAKETHIS line on a peer session the next wire event is an :article (or the close), so no article line is ever a command. Touches fn-peer-command and peer-inbound-invariants; wants the proofs lane or a peering slice.
scenario: A streaming peer (INN with laxmid, or any sender whose Message-ID is over 250 octets or outside fn-af-msg-id-corep) sends 'TAKETHIS <odd id>' then the article. fn answers 501, then reads every header and body line as a command on the PEER session: each draws a reply the sender maps onto its later outstanding CHECK/TAKETHIS (the stream desynchronises, answers land on the wrong Message-IDs), and a body line such as 'TAKETHIS <x@y>' starts a new transfer whose article is the rest of the body (dot-unstuffed), stored as relayed from that peer. The article's author, not the peer, chooses those lines.
title: TAKETHIS whose argument fails fn's Message-ID grammar is answered 501 and its article is then executed line by line as commands on the peer session
